statement: AMD put its Helios rack-scale system into production and named anchor deployments including Anthropic taking up to 2 gigawatts of MI455X GPUs in Helios racks and OpenAI bringing Helios online from Q4 2026.
why: Named gigawatt-scale commitments from frontier labs are the clearest sign yet that a credible second merchant source of AI accelerators is reaching production, which changes buyers' options.

impact.mechanism: Production Helios racks with named frontier-lab commitments add non-Nvidia accelerator supply and design wins, easing buyer dependence on one vendor while adding to the same upstream memory, packaging and power draw.

evidence.excerpt: deploying up to 2 gigawatts of MI455X GPUs in Helios racks
up to 30% more tokens per dollar than the competition

confidence.basis: Primary vendor press release naming specific partners and deployment timing; the performance and gigawatt claims are vendor-stated and capped by 'up to' language.

dispersion: Anthropic's commitment is phrased as 'up to' 2 gigawatts and Meta is only validating and testing, so committed volume is not firm.
